newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African June trade surplus helped by oil, gems.
newsitem.headline: S.African June trade surplus helped by oil, gems.

text.p: Ballooning exports and only a moderate increase in imports heaved South Africa's trade balance into a 4.15 billion rand in surplus in June.

But the data was helped by the exclusion of one billion rand's worth of oil imports and the inclusion of around two billion rand's worth of Botswana diamond exports, which pointed to a lower surplus in July, economists said.

The South African Revenue Services said earlier that South Africa's trade balance -- which includes data for neighbouring Botswana, Namibia, Swaziland and Lesotho -- swelled to 4.15 billion rand in the month from 1.75 billion rand in May.
It added, however, that one billion rand's worth of oil imports had been excluded from the latest balance and would be included in July's data.
Despite this, and what E.W. Balderson economist Mike Schussler estimated to be a two billion rand contribution from Botswana diamond exports, economists said the data was impressive.
"It is an amazing figure. Totally unexpected," E.W. Balderson economist Mike Schussler said.
"If more or less two billion rand from Botswana diamonds comes out and the one billion rand is added to the oil imports, you have what economists were expecting," Schussler said.
A Reuters consensus poll of economists forecast a surplus of 1.28 billion rand for the month.

"The figures are very impressive if one looks at cumulative export figures which are up almost 25 percent year-on-year. That way outstrips import growth," Barnard, Jacobs Mellet economist Chantal Friedman said.
Cumulative exports for the year to date were pegged at 68.34 billion rand from 54.64 billion rand in May and 53.94 billion rand in June last year.

"Exports went into a bit of a lull at one stage but they seem to be picking up again and I would definitely expect that the trade surplus for this year is going to be far bigger than it was last year," Friedman added.
